How a Poisoned Security Scanner Became the Key to Backdooring LiteLLM

Snyk
2026-03-24 14 use cases 6 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

On March 24, 2026, threat actor known as TeamPCP published backdoored versions of the litellm Python package after stealing PyPI credentials via a compromised Trivy GitHub Action in LiteLLM's CI/CD pipeline. Here's what happened, how the three-stage malware works, and how to check if you're affected.

[LLM] Malicious litellm 1.82.7/1.82.8 wheel install drops litellm_init.pth in site-packages Delivery High
Detects installation of the trojanized litellm PyPI versions 1.82.7 or 1.82.8 by spotting the diagnostic file litellm_init.pth being written into a Python site-packages directory (an unusual artefact name for legitimate packages) and/or pip writing litellm-1.82.7/litellm-1.82.8 .dist-info metadata. Versions 1.82.6 and earlier are clean. Rationale: Anchored on the article's explicit artefact litellm_init.pth (34,628 bytes) dropped into site-packages and the two malicious wheel versions 1.82.7 / 1.82.8. The file name is novel to this campaign and the dist-info paths are version-pinned, giving high fidelity. Cross-checked: PyPI advisory SNYK-PYTHON-LITELLM-15762713 and the FutureSearch disclosure both confirm the file name and sizes. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-PYTHON-LITELLM-15762713 • https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/24518

   or (FolderPath has_any ("litellm-1.82.7.dist-info", "litellm-1.82.8.dist-info"))
   or (FileName =~ "litellm_init.pth" and FileSize between (30000 .. 40000))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, FileSize, SHA256,

| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Python .pth startup hook executes subprocess to curl C2 (litellm fork-bomb pattern) Installation High
Detects the .pth-triggered execution chain unique to litellm 1.82.8: python(1) spawning python(2) (because the .pth re-fires on each interpreter), which in turn spawns curl or openssl to package and POST tpcp.tar.gz to models.litellm.cloud. The python→python→curl/openssl tree is what produced the RAM-exhaustion symptom McMahon reported. Rationale: Article-specific anchors: (a) python parent — because the .pth fires from the interpreter, (b) curl/openssl/tar child — the verbatim exfil stack named in the article, (c) the literal strings models.litellm.cloud, tpcp.tar.gz, session.key.enc, payload.enc. Generic python-spawns-curl is too noisy; the three IOC strings give the article-specific lift. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/poisoned-security-scanner-backdooring-litellm/ • https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/24518
ATT&CKT1546.018 T1059.006

DeviceProcessEvents

| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","python.exe","python3.exe")
| where (FileName in~ ("curl","curl.exe","openssl","openssl.exe","tar","tar.exe"))
   and (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("models.litellm.cloud","tpcp.tar.gz","session.key","payload.enc","session.key.enc")
        or ProcessCommandLine has "AES-256-CBC" and ProcessCommandLine has "-pbkdf2")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,

| where SyslogMessage has_any ("curl","openssl","python")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, ProcessName, ProcessID, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] DNS / HTTPS egress to TeamPCP exfil infra (models.litellm.cloud, checkmarx.zone) Command & Control High
Detects any host in the org resolving or connecting to the two TeamPCP-controlled exfil domains used across the litellm, Trivy, and Checkmarx KICS operations. Both domains were registered in March 2026 (models.litellm.cloud on Mar 23) — any resolution within or after that window is highly suspicious. Rationale: Direct IOC match on the exfil and C2 domains/IP that Wiz, Endor Labs, and Snyk all corroborate (same RSA key fingerprint across litellm/Trivy/KICS payloads). These domains have no benign legitimate use — registered Mar 23 2026 specifically for this campaign — so any hit is high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/poisoned-security-scanner-backdooring-litellm/ • https://www.endorlabs.com/learn/teampcp • https://www.wiz.io/blog/teampcp-supply-chain

[LLM] Exfil staging artefacts: session.key, payload.enc, session.key.enc, tpcp.tar.gz in temp Actions on Objectives High
Detects the four staging files the TeamPCP payload creates in the system temp directory while building the encrypted exfil bundle (AES-256-CBC session key wrapped with their RSA-4096 OAEP public key, archived as tpcp.tar.gz). All four names are hardcoded in the malware and shared across litellm / Trivy / KICS operations. Rationale: All four filenames (tpcp.tar.gz, session.key, payload.enc, session.key.enc) are quoted verbatim from the article's Stage 2 description. Wiz confirmed identical RSA public key across litellm/Trivy/KICS, meaning these staging names are reused across all three campaigns — extremely low FP rate. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/poisoned-security-scanner-backdooring-litellm/ • https://www.wiz.io/blog/teampcp-supply-chain
ATT&CKT1560.001 T1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("tpcp.tar.gz","session.key","session.key.enc","payload.enc")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp),
            Files=make_set(FileName), DistinctFiles=dcount(FileName),
            Procs=make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName),
            CmdLines=make_set(InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
            Paths=make_set(FolderPath)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| where DistinctFiles >= 2 or array_index_of(Files, "tpcp.tar.gz") >= 0
| order by FirstSeen desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("tpcp.tar.gz","session.key.enc","payload.enc")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, ProcessName, ProcessID, SyslogMessage
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated),
            Procs=make_set(ProcessName), MsgSample=any(SyslogMessage),
            Hits=count()
          by Computer, HostName
| order by FirstSeen desc

[LLM] TeamPCP Linux credential harvest: Python reading /etc/shadow + auth.log + cloud Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the Stage 1 collection behaviour: a python process opening a high-fan-out set of sensitive Linux credential stores (/etc/shadow, /var/log/auth.log, ~/.ssh/, ~/.aws/, ~/.azure/, ~/.config/gcloud/, ~/.kube/, ~/.docker/config.json, .env, cryptocurrency wallets) within a short window — characteristic of the litellm 1.82.7/1.82.8 grabber, not a normal interpreter session. Rationale: The article lists the exact files/paths the Stage 1 grabber touches; we anchor on that high-fan-out set (≥3 distinct sensitive paths from a python interpreter within 7d) rather than any single path, which avoids generic /etc/shadow noise from sysadmins. The IMDS string 169.254.169.254 is included because the article explicitly calls out direct IMDS queries. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/poisoned-security-scanner-backdooring-litellm/
ATT&CKT1003.008 T1552.001 T1552.004 T1552.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let SensitivePaths = dynamic([
    "/etc/shadow", "/var/log/auth.log",
    "/.ssh/id_", "/.ssh/authorized_keys",
    "/.aws/credentials", "/.aws/config",
    "/.azure/", "/.config/gcloud/",
    "/.kube/config", "/.docker/config.json",
    "/.env", "wallet.dat", "/.bitcoin/", "/.ethereum/keystore/", "/.solana/", "/.cardano/", "/Ledger/"
  ]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed","FileAccessed")
   or ActionType has "File"
| extend MatchedPath = tostring(SensitivePaths[0])
| extend Hits = array_length(set_intersect(SensitivePaths, pack_array(FolderPath)))
| where FolderPath has_any (SensitivePaths) or FileName has_any ("shadow","auth.log","credentials","kubeconfig","wallet.dat")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp),
            DistinctSensitivePaths=dcount(FolderPath),
            PathsSample=make_set(FolderPath, 25),
            Cmd=any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessId
| where DistinctSensitivePaths >= 3
| order by FirstSeen desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Facility in ("auth","authpriv","daemon","user","kern")
| where ProcessName matches regex @"(?i)^python[0-9]?$"
   or SyslogMessage has_any ("python","python3")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("/etc/shadow","/var/log/auth.log","/.ssh/id_","/.aws/credentials","/.aws/config","/.azure/","/.config/gcloud/","/.kube/config","/.docker/config.json","wallet.dat","/.bitcoin/","/.ethereum/keystore/","169.254.169.254")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated),
            Hits=count(),
            DistinctIndicators=dcount(extract(@"(/etc/shadow|/var/log/auth\.log|/\.ssh/id_|/\.aws/credentials|/\.aws/config|/\.azure/|/\.config/gcloud/|/\.kube/config|/\.docker/config\.json|wallet\.dat|/\.bitcoin/|/\.ethereum/keystore/|169\.254\.169\.254)", 0, SyslogMessage)),
            Sample=any(SyslogMessage),
            Procs=make_set(ProcessName)
          by Computer, HostName
| where DistinctIndicators >= 3
| order by FirstSeen desc
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:(PATH OR EXECVE) @process.name:(python OR python3) (@file.path:(/etc/shadow OR /var/log/auth.log OR */.ssh/id_* OR */.aws/credentials OR */.aws/config OR */.azure/* OR */.config/gcloud/* OR */.kube/config OR */.docker/config.json OR */.env OR */wallet.dat OR */.bitcoin/* OR */.ethereum/keystore/*) OR @process.command_line:(*\/etc\/shadow* OR *\/var\/log\/auth.log* OR *169.254.169.254*))
(#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo OR #event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2)
| (ContextImageFileName=/python(3)?$/i OR ImageFileName=/python(3)?$/i)
| (TargetFileName=/\/etc\/shadow$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/var\/log\/auth\.log$/i OR TargetFileName=/\.ssh\/id_/i OR TargetFileName=/\.aws\/(credentials|config)$/i OR TargetFileName=/\.azure\//i OR TargetFileName=/\.config\/gcloud\//i OR TargetFileName=/\.kube\/config$/i OR TargetFileName=/\.docker\/config\.json$/i OR TargetFileName=/wallet\.dat$/i OR TargetFileName=/\.ethereum\/keystore/i OR CommandLine=/169\.254\.169\.254/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName], function=count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true), limit=200)
| _count >= 3
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name IN ("python","python3") AND (Filesystem.file_path="/etc/shadow" OR Filesystem.file_path="/var/log/auth.log" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/config" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.azure/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gcloud/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.kube/config" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.docker/config.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.env" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/wallet.dat" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.bitcoin/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ethereum/keystore/*") by host Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | stats min(firstTime) as firstTime values(paths) as touched_paths dc(file_path) as distinct_sensitive_paths by host user process_name | where distinct_sensitive_paths >= 3 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name IN ("python","python3") AND (Filesystem.file_path="/etc/shadow" OR Filesystem.file_path="/var/log/auth.log" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/config" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.azure/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gcloud/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.kube/config" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.docker/config.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.env" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/wallet.dat" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.bitcoin/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ethereum/keystore/*") by host Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | stats min(firstTime) as firstTime values(paths) as touched_paths dc(file_path) as distinct_sensitive_paths by host user process_name | where distinct_sensitive_paths >= 3 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web

    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"

    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",

         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]

Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Cloudflare-tunnel curl-piped Python stager (kamikaze.sh / kube.py)
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — CanisterWorm Gets Teeth: TeamPCP's Kubernetes Wiper Targets Iran
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Malicious privileged DaemonSet apply in kube-system (host-provisioner-iran / host-provisioner-std / kamikaze) · [LLM] CanisterWorm persistence: pglog/pg_state/internal-monitor systemd unit and /tmp/pglog drop · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] DNS/HTTP egress to CanisterWorm ICP canister C2 (tdtqy-oyaaa-aaaae-af2dq-cai) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Host-root mount wiper: chroot /mnt/host reboot -f or rm -rf / --no-preserve-root · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] DNS/HTTP egress to CanisterWorm ICP canister C2 (tdtqy-oyaaa-aaaae-af2dq-cai) Command & Control High
Hunts for lookups or connections to the TeamPCP CanisterWorm Internet Computer Protocol canister at tdtqy-oyaaa-aaaae-af2dq-cai.raw.icp0.io. The reused canister is the C2 endpoint that the Kubernetes wiper variant's installed backdoor polls every 50 minutes, so any DNS or HTTP touch is a high-confidence indicator of TeamPCP presence. Rationale: The canister ID tdtqy-oyaaa-aaaae-af2dq-cai is unique to TeamPCP's CanisterWorm family (Aikido + earlier CanisterWorm writeups), so any traffic to that subdomain is essentially zero-FP. The ICP raw subdomain is the documented poll path; canister reuse across the Trivy compromise and Kubernetes variants is corroborated in the Aikido CanisterWorm post. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/teampcp-stage-payload-canisterworm-iran • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1102/002/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004 T1102.002

   or AdditionalFields has "tdtqy-oyaaa-aaaae-af2dq-cai"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, LocalIP
| order by Timestamp desc
let canister = "tdtqy-oyaaa-aaaae-af2dq-cai";
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DnsQuery has canister or DnsQuery endswith ".raw.icp0.io"
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, SrcHost = SrcHostname, SrcIp = SrcIpAddr, Query = DnsQuery, Vendor = EventVendor),
  (DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Name has canister or Name endswith ".raw.icp0.io"
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, SrcHost = "", SrcIp = ClientIP, Query = Name, Vendor = "MicrosoftDNS"),
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where RequestURL has canister or DestinationHostName has canister or DestinationDnsDomain has canister
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = SourceHostName, SrcHost = SourceHostName, SrcIp = SourceIP, Query = coalesce(RequestURL, DestinationHostName, DestinationDnsDomain), Vendor = DeviceVendor),
  (Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where SyslogMessage has canister
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, SrcHost = HostName, SrcIp = HostIP, Query = SyslogMessage, Vendor = "Syslog")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Cloudflare-tunnel curl-piped Python stager (kamikaze.sh / kube.py) Delivery High
Hunts for the TeamPCP wiper stager that downloads kamikaze.sh / kube.py from a trycloudflare.com tunnel and pipes the output into python3 (`curl -L -s <url> | python3 -`). Anchored on the verbatim filenames and tunnel hostnames Aikido observed. Rationale: Anchored on the verbatim stager URLs and filenames (kamikaze.sh, kube.py, both Cloudflare tunnel hostnames) Aikido captured, combined with the curl/wget|python3 binary set. Legitimate use of these exact filenames from these exact tunnels is implausible. [LLM] Malicious privileged DaemonSet apply in kube-system (host-provisioner-iran / host-provisioner-std / kamikaze) Installation High
Hunts for creation of the TeamPCP DaemonSets named host-provisioner-iran (wiper) or host-provisioner-std (backdoor installer) in kube-system, including the privileged hostPath `/` mount and kamikaze container name. Detects at apply time so the iran variant can be stopped before chroot reboot fires across nodes. Rationale: Anchored on three article-verbatim DaemonSet/container names (host-provisioner-iran, host-provisioner-std, kamikaze) with no legitimate counterpart, plus the privileged + hostPath + /mnt/host pattern unique to host-escape containers. Detects at apply time — before the wiper container schedules and chroot reboot fires. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/teampcp-stage-payload-canisterworm-iran • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1610/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1611/

[LLM] Host-root mount wiper: chroot /mnt/host reboot -f or rm -rf / --no-preserve-root Actions on Objectives High
Hunts for execution of the TeamPCP wiper commands inside a privileged container or directly on the host: `find /mnt/host -maxdepth 1 -not -name 'mnt' -exec rm -rf` followed by `chroot /mnt/host reboot -f`, or the non-K8s poison-pill `rm -rf / --no-preserve-root`. Rationale: Three command-line signatures pulled verbatim from the kamikaze container args and poison_pill() function in kube.py. None of these strings have a legitimate operational counterpart — `--no-preserve-root` exists specifically to override the safety check, and `chroot /mnt/host reboot -f` is only seen when a privileged container is forcibly rebooting its host. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/teampcp-stage-payload-canisterworm-iran • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1485/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1611/
ATT&CKT1485 T1561.002 T1611 T1529
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "rm -rf / --no-preserve-root"
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "chroot" and ProcessCommandLine has "/mnt/host" and ProcessCommandLine has "reboot")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "find /mnt/host" and ProcessCommandLine has "-exec rm -rf")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "rm -rf / --no-preserve-root"
       or (ActingProcessCommandLine has "chroot" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "/mnt/host" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "reboot")
       or (ActingProcessCommandLine has "find /mnt/host" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "-exec rm -rf")
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, User = ActorUsername, Proc = ActingProcessName, Cmd = ActingProcessCommandLine, Parent = ParentProcessName),
  (Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where SyslogMessage has "rm -rf / --no-preserve-root"
       or (SyslogMessage has "chroot" and SyslogMessage has "/mnt/host" and SyslogMessage has "reboot")
       or (SyslogMessage has "find /mnt/host" and SyslogMessage has "-exec rm -rf")
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, User = "", Proc = ProcessName, Cmd = SyslogMessage, Parent = "")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*rm -rf / --no-preserve-root*" OR (Processes.process="*chroot*" AND Processes.process="*/mnt/host*" AND Processes.process="*reboot*") OR (Processes.process="*find /mnt/host*" AND Processes.process="*-exec rm -rf*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
[LLM] CanisterWorm persistence: pglog/pg_state/internal-monitor systemd unit and /tmp/pglog drop Installation High
Hunts for the CanisterWorm backdoor's host-side persistence — the runner.py drop into /tmp/pglog (CONFIG['TARGET_DIR']) and the systemd unit named pglog / pg_state / internal-monitor (PostgreSQL-themed decoy names) wired with `ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 .../runner.py` and `Description=System Monitor`. Rationale: Article-verbatim service names (pglog, pg_state, internal-monitor — PostgreSQL-themed masquerade per Aikido + earlier CanisterWorm post), drop path (/tmp/pglog), and the unique unit fields `Description=System Monitor` + `ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 .../runner.py`. No legitimate PostgreSQL tooling exists at those names with that ExecStart binary. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/teampcp-stage-payload-canisterworm-iran • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1543/002/
ATT&CKT1543.002 T1036.005 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
union isfuzzy=true
  (DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where (FolderPath has "/etc/systemd/system/" and FileName in~ ("pglog.service","pg_state.service","internal-monitor.service"))
        or FolderPath startswith "/tmp/pglog"
        or (FolderPath has "/tmp/" and FileName =~ "runner.py")
    | extend Evt = "FileWrite", Detail = strcat(FolderPath, FileName), Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Bin = InitiatingProcessFileName),
  (DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("systemctl enable --now pglog","systemctl enable --now pg_state","systemctl enable --now internal-monitor")
         or (ProcessCommandLine has "Description=System Monitor" and ProcessCommandLine has "ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3")
    | extend Evt = "ProcessExec", Detail = ProcessCommandLine, Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Bin = FileName)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, Evt, Detail, Bin, Cmd
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where (TargetFilePath has "/etc/systemd/system/" and TargetFileName in~ ("pglog.service","pg_state.service","internal-monitor.service"))
        or TargetFilePath startswith "/tmp/pglog"
        or (TargetFilePath has "/tmp/" and TargetFileName =~ "runner.py")
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, User = ActorUsername, Evt = "FileWrite", Detail = TargetFilePath, Proc = ActingProcessName, Cmd = ActingProcessCommandLine),
  (ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("systemctl enable --now pglog","systemctl enable --now pg_state","systemctl enable --now internal-monitor")
         or (ActingProcessCommandLine has "Description=System Monitor" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3")
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, User = ActorUsername, Evt = "ProcessExec", Detail = ActingProcessCommandLine, Proc = ActingProcessName, Cmd = ActingProcessCommandLine),
  (Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where SyslogMessage has_any ("pglog.service","pg_state.service","internal-monitor.service")
        and SyslogMessage has_any ("systemd","enabled","started")
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, User = "", Evt = "SyslogUnit", Detail = SyslogMessage, Proc = ProcessName, Cmd = SyslogMessage)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: CanisterWorm pglog/pg_state/internal-monitor Systemd Persistence
id: 4f8a1c3b-7d5e-4f29-a1b2-9c0d6e3f8a44
description: Detects CanisterWorm backdoor systemd persistence (pglog / pg_state / internal-monitor unit files) or the runner.py drop in /tmp/pglog used by the TeamPCP Kubernetes wiper variant
references:
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/teampcp-stage-payload-canisterworm-iran
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1543.002
  - attack.t1036.005
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: linux
detection:
  unit_file:
    TargetFilename:
      - '/etc/systemd/system/pglog.service'
      - '/etc/systemd/system/pg_state.service'
      - '/etc/systemd/system/internal-monitor.service'
  runner_drop:
    TargetFilename|startswith: '/tmp/pglog'
  condition: unit_file or runner_drop
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate PostgreSQL logging tool genuinely named pglog (rare; verify ExecStart points at /usr/bin/python3 .../runner.py)
level: high
source:(linux.auditd OR linux.syslog) ((@file.path:("/etc/systemd/system/pglog.service" OR "/etc/systemd/system/pg_state.service" OR "/etc/systemd/system/internal-monitor.service") OR @file.path:/tmp/pglog/*) OR @process.command_line:("*systemctl enable --now pglog*" OR "*systemctl enable --now pg_state*" OR "*systemctl enable --now internal-monitor*" OR ("*Description=System Monitor*" AND "*ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3*")))
(#event_simpleName=FileWritten (TargetFileName=/\/etc\/systemd\/system\/(pglog|pg_state|internal-monitor)\.service$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/tmp\/pglog/i OR TargetFileName=/\/tmp\/.*runner\.py$/i))
OR (#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 (CommandLine=/systemctl\s+enable\s+--now\s+(pglog|pg_state|internal-monitor)/i OR CommandLine=/Description=System Monitor/i))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="/etc/systemd/system/pglog.service" OR Filesystem.file_path="/etc/systemd/system/pg_state.service" OR Filesystem.file_path="/etc/systemd/system/internal-monitor.service" OR Filesystem.file_path="/tmp/pglog/*" OR (Filesystem.file_name="runner.py" AND Filesystem.file_path="/tmp/*")) by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | append [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*systemctl enable --now pglog*" OR Processes.process="*systemctl enable --now pg_state*" OR Processes.process="*systemctl enable --now internal-monitor*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`]
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Crypto-Wallet Keystore Access by Non-Wallet Process
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d02
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers / wallet drainers read keystore files from MetaMask,
    Exodus, Atomic, Phantom, Bitcoin, Electrum, Ethereum-cli wallets.
    Filtering out the legitimate wallet binaries leaves only attacker
    activity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1005/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1005
    - attack.collection
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Ethereum\keystore\'
            - '\Bitcoin\'
            - '\Exodus\'
            - '\Electrum\wallets\'
            - '\MetaMask\'
            - '\Phantom\'
            - '\Atomic\Local Storage\'
    filter_legit:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\MetaMask.exe'
            - '\Exodus.exe'
            - '\Atomic.exe'
            - '\electrum.exe'
            - '\Bitcoin.exe'
            - '\Phantom.exe'

falsepositives:
    - Backup software
level: high

        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"

| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem

logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,

| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:

            - '\pwsh.exe'

            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'

ATT&CKT1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Registry
// Article-specific bespoke detection — CanisterWorm Gets Teeth: TeamPCP's Kubernetes Wiper Targets Iran
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("kube.py", "pgmon.py", "proxy.sh", "pcpcat.py"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FolderPath has_any ("/tmp/pglog", "/usr/bin/env", "/dev/null", "/tmp/kubectl", "/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount", "/etc/timezone", "/usr/bin/python3", "/var/lib/svc_internal/runner.py") or FileName in~ ("kube.py", "pgmon.py", "proxy.sh", "pcpcat.py"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — TeamPCP deploys CanisterWorm on NPM following Trivy compromise
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"

| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest

| sort - count

title: Crypto-Wallet Keystore Access by Non-Wallet Process
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d02
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers / wallet drainers read keystore files from MetaMask,
    Exodus, Atomic, Phantom, Bitcoin, Electrum, Ethereum-cli wallets.
    Filtering out the legitimate wallet binaries leaves only attacker
    activity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1005/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1005
    - attack.collection
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Ethereum\keystore\'
            - '\Bitcoin\'
            - '\Exodus\'
            - '\Electrum\wallets\'
            - '\MetaMask\'
            - '\Phantom\'
            - '\Atomic\Local Storage\'
    filter_legit:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\MetaMask.exe'
            - '\Exodus.exe'
            - '\Atomic.exe'
            - '\electrum.exe'
            - '\Bitcoin.exe'
            - '\Phantom.exe'
    condition: selection_path and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
    - Backup software
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003

DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Article-specific behavioural hunt — TeamPCP deploys CanisterWorm on NPM following Trivy compromise Exploitation High
Auto-generated hunt targeting the specific binaries, paths, registry locations and command-line fragments named in this article. Hunting tier — needs analyst review and environment tuning before promotion to alerting.
ATT&CKT1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Registry
// Article-specific bespoke detection — TeamPCP deploys CanisterWorm on NPM following Trivy compromise
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("node.js", "deploy.js", "service.py", "sysmon.py", "index.js"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

// File-creation events for the named binaries / paths
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FolderPath has_any ("/usr/bin/python3", "/tmp/pglog", "/tmp/.pg_state", "/usr/bin/env", "/etc/npmrc", "/dev/null") or FileName in~ ("node.js", "deploy.js", "service.py", "sysmon.py", "index.js"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-43520")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

[LLM] BYOVD: Genshin Impact mhyprot.sys driver dropped/loaded outside legitimate game install (Embargo evil-mhyprot-cli) Installation High
Hunts the BYOVD pattern called out in the ESET article where the Embargo gang shifted to the public evil-mhyprot-cli PoC, which abuses the Genshin Impact anti-cheat driver mhyprot.sys / mhyprot2.sys to terminate protected processes from kernel context. Signal is the driver file landing on disk or being registered as a service anywhere other than a legitimate miHoYo / Genshin Impact install path. Rationale: Article names evil-mhyprot-cli explicitly as Embargo's current EDR killer. The driver filenames mhyprot.sys / mhyprot2.sys and the SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\mhyprot key are well-documented BYOVD artefacts; flagging them outside legitimate Genshin Impact paths is high-fidelity because no business workflow drops this driver elsewhere. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/kkent030315/evil-mhyprot-cli • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/edr-killers-explained-beyond-the-drivers/ • https://www.loldrivers.io/drivers/
ATT&CKT1068 T1562.001 T1014

  | where FileName in~ ("mhyprot.sys","mhyprot2.sys")
  | where not(FolderPath has_any (_legit_paths))
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
            InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
            InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source="FileWrite"
),
(
  DeviceRegistryEvents

      or (RegistryValueName =~ "ImagePath" and RegistryValueData has_any ("mhyprot.sys","mhyprot2.sys"))
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData,
            InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
            InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source="ServiceReg"
)
| order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] EDRSilencer-style WFP filter blocking outbound traffic from named EDR binaries Installation Medium
Hunts the driverless EDR-disruption technique highlighted by ESET as gaining quick ransomware adoption: EDRSilencer (and clones) install persistent Windows Filtering Platform filters that drop outbound traffic for EDR sensor binaries (MsMpEng.exe, MsSense.exe, SentinelAgent.exe, CSFalconService.exe, ekrn.exe, etc.). Detection ties WFP block events (EID 5157) to known EDR binary paths and cross-references unusual processes loading FWPUCLNT.dll. Rationale: Article specifically calls out EDRSilencer (and EDR-Freeze) as the rapidly-adopted driverless class. Detection pivots on the technique invariant: WFP-layer drops of outbound traffic from named EDR sensor binaries — Trend Micro and Mahmoud Elfawair's hunting writeup both confirm EID 5157 + EDR application-name as the high-fidelity signal. Sigma is omitted because the detection is a count/window correlation rather than single-event-shape. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/netero1010/EDRSilencer • https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/24/j/edrsilencer-disrupting-endpoint-security-solutions.html • https://github.com/amjcyber/EDRNoiseMaker • https://www.csoonline.com/article/3567074/attackers-repurpose-edrsilencer-to-evade-detection.html
ATT&CKT1562.004 T1562.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let _edr_binaries = dynamic(["MsMpEng.exe","MsSense.exe","MsSenseS.exe","SenseIR.exe","SentinelAgent.exe","SentinelServiceHost.exe","CSFalconService.exe","CSFalconContainer.exe","ekrn.exe","egui.exe","elastic-agent.exe","xagt.exe","cb.exe","RepMgr.exe","bdservicehost.exe","cyserver.exe","cytray.exe","qualysagent.exe","TmListen.exe","PccNTMon.exe"]);
let _edr_binaries_lower = _edr_binaries | mv-apply b=_edr_binaries to typeof(string) on (project tolower(b));
union
(
  // Direct execution of the EDRSilencer tool / clones
  DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where FileName =~ "EDRSilencer.exe"
     or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("FwpmFilterAdd0","FwpmEngineOpen0")
     or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_all ("New-NetFirewallRule","Block","Outbound") and ProcessCommandLine has_any (_edr_binaries))
     or (FileName =~ "netsh.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "wfp" and ProcessCommandLine has "add")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
            ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName,
            InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source="ToolExec"
),
(
  // Non-EDR processes loading the WFP user-mode client (FWPUCLNT.DLL) - rare outside Defender/firewall control panel
  DeviceImageLoadEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where FileName =~ "FWPUCLNT.DLL"
  | where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\"
      and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files\"
  | where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("netsh.exe","MsMpEng.exe","svchost.exe","explorer.exe","mmc.exe","WerFault.exe")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName,
            InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
            InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source="WfpDllLoad"
)
| order by Timestamp desc
let _edr_binaries = dynamic([@"\MsMpEng.exe",@"\MsSense.exe",@"\MsSenseS.exe",@"\SenseIR.exe",@"\SentinelAgent.exe",@"\SentinelServiceHost.exe",@"\CSFalconService.exe",@"\CSFalconContainer.exe",@"\ekrn.exe",@"\egui.exe",@"\elastic-agent.exe",@"\xagt.exe",@"\cb.exe",@"\RepMgr.exe",@"\bdservicehost.exe",@"\cyserver.exe",@"\TmListen.exe",@"\PccNTMon.exe"]);
// EID 5157 = WFP blocked an outbound connection. Burst of blocks for EDR binaries == EDRSilencer pattern.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where EventID in (5157, 5152)
| extend Application = tostring(extract(@"Application Name:\s*([^\r\n]+)", 1, EventData))
| where isnotempty(Application)
| where Application has_any (_edr_binaries)
| summarize BlockCount = count(),
            DistinctEdrBinaries = dcount(Application),
            BlockedApps = make_set(Application, 10),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by Computer, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
| where BlockCount >= 20 or DistinctEdrBinaries >= 2
| order by LastSeen desc

[LLM] EDR-Freeze: WerFaultSecure.exe abused to suspend AV/EDR processes via MiniDumpWriteDump race Installation High
Hunts the EDR-Freeze technique that ESET highlights as a fast-adopted driverless EDR killer. The attack spawns the PPL-protected WerFaultSecure.exe to invoke MiniDumpWriteDump against an EDR/AV process (which suspends the target's threads), then suspends WerFaultSecure itself so the threads are never resumed — leaving the security agent in a coma. Signal: WerFaultSecure spawned by a non-WER parent with a PID/handle argument that resolves to a known EDR/AV binary, or NtSuspendProcess against WerFaultSecure from a non-system caller. Rationale: Article calls out EDR-Freeze by name as a rapidly-adopted driverless EDR killer. Microsoft's MAPP signature Behavior:Win32/EDRFreeze.A, Picus Security, BinaryDefense ARC Labs, and BleepingComputer all confirm the same invariant: WerFaultSecure.exe spawned by a non-WER parent with dump-style arguments, plus an NtSuspendProcess against WerFaultSecure itself. That parent-anomaly is the highest-fidelity, lowest-FP shape available for this technique today. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/new-edr-freeze-tool-uses-windows-wer-to-suspend-security-software/ • https://www.picussecurity.com/resource/blog/edr-freeze-the-user-mode-attack-that-puts-security-into-a-coma • https://binarydefense.com/resources/blog/dont-freeze-me-out-bro-arc-labs-technical-analysis-of-edr-freeze • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=Behavior:Win32/EDRFreeze.A • https://detection.fyi/sigmahq/sigma/windows/process_creation/proc_creation_win_hktl_edr_freeze/
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1055
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let _trusted_wer_parents = dynamic(["svchost.exe","wermgr.exe","werfault.exe","services.exe","smss.exe","csrss.exe","taskhostw.exe","sihost.exe"]);
let WerFaultSpawn =
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName =~ "WerFaultSecure.exe"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ (_trusted_wer_parents)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
              ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName,
              ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              ParentFolder = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
              ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
              ChildPid = ProcessId, Signal="WerFaultSecure_unusual_parent";
let SuspendOnWer =
    DeviceEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType in ("OpenProcessApiCall","SuspendThread","ProcessPrimaryTokenModified")
    | where FileName =~ "WerFaultSecure.exe"      // target was WerFaultSecure
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ (_trusted_wer_parents)
    | where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\System32"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              Signal="Suspend_against_WerFaultSecure";
union WerFaultSpawn, SuspendOnWer
| order by Timestamp desc
let _trusted_wer_parents = dynamic(["svchost.exe","wermgr.exe","werfault.exe","services.exe","smss.exe","csrss.exe","taskhostw.exe","sihost.exe"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(
  SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where NewProcessName endswith @"\WerFaultSecure.exe"
  | extend ParentLeaf = tostring(split(ParentProcessName, @"\")[-1])
  | where tolower(ParentLeaf) !in (_trusted_wer_parents)

(

  | where tolower(ParentLeaf) !in (_trusted_wer_parents)
