Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High

ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — GlassWorm Hides a RAT Inside a Malicious Chrome Extension
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] GlassWorm Stage-3 RAT installation under %APPDATA%\QtCvyfVWKH\index.js · [LLM] GlassWorm Stage-3a UpdateLedger Run-key persistence pointing at %TEMP%\SKuyzYcDD.exe · Suspicious browser extension installation · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] GlassWorm hardcoded C2 IP egress (45.32.150.251 / 217.69.3.152) for Stage-2 fetch and exfil · [LLM] GlassWorm Solana blockchain dead-drop C2 lookup via public RPC endpoints from Node · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] GlassWorm Stage-3a Ledger impersonator binary execution (SHA256 06fab21d / SKuyzYcDD.exe) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process
[LLM] GlassWorm hardcoded C2 IP egress (45.32.150.251 / 217.69.3.152) for Stage-2 fetch and exfil Command & Control High
Detects any host reaching the GlassWorm Stage-2 / Stage-3 delivery and exfil IPs documented in the Aikido write-up. Stage-2 payload is POSTed to http://217.69.3.152/wall and Stage-3 binaries are fetched from 45.32.150.251 with an os: header. Rationale: Anchored on the four hardcoded IPs explicitly named by Aikido (45.32.150.251 serves Stage-2/3 payloads, 217.69.3.152/wall is the Stage-2 exfil endpoint, 217.69.0.159 + 45.150.34.158 listed in the pre-extracted IOC bundle). IP-level egress is a smoking gun with effectively zero legitimate use. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/glassworm-chrome-extension-rat
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in ("45.32.150.251","217.69.3.152","217.69.0.159","45.150.34.158")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, LocalIP
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr in ("45.32.150.251","217.69.3.152","217.69.0.159","45.150.34.158")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol, EventProduct, EventVendor
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] GlassWorm Stage-3 RAT installation under %APPDATA%\QtCvyfVWKH\index.js Installation High
Detects creation of the persistent Stage-3 RAT module GlassWorm drops at %APPDATA%\QtCvyfVWKH\index.js along with its companion native modules (c_x64.node, f_ex86.node, index_ia32.node, index_x64.node, w.node, data). This folder name is a high-fidelity, attacker-specific artifact. Rationale: %APPDATA%\QtCvyfVWKH\index.js is the exact persistent-RAT install path named in the Aikido article, and the five .node module names (c_x64, f_ex86, index_ia32, index_x64, w) are unique GlassWorm artifacts — none collide with mainstream Node.js dependencies. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/glassworm-chrome-extension-rat
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1105 T1547.001

[LLM] GlassWorm Stage-3a UpdateLedger Run-key persistence pointing at %TEMP%\SKuyzYcDD.exe Installation High
Detects the HKCU Run-key entry UpdateLedger that GlassWorm's Stage-3a Ledger-Live impersonator creates, and the unsigned .NET WPF binary it drops at %TEMP%\SKuyzYcDD.exe (Assaac.exe / LLC LogicSub). Rationale: UpdateLedger as a Run-key value name is unique to GlassWorm's Stage-3a per Aikido, and SKuyzYcDD.exe is the exact drop name in %TEMP%. Both strings have effectively zero benign collisions. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/glassworm-chrome-extension-rat
ATT&CKT1547.001 T1036.005

[LLM] GlassWorm Solana blockchain dead-drop C2 lookup via public RPC endpoints from Node Command & Control Medium
Detects DNS / connection activity from node.exe (or other non-browser process) to the nine public Solana RPC endpoints the GlassWorm loader cycles through to retrieve its Stage-2 URL from a transaction memo field. This is the loader's only network step before fetching Stage-2. Rationale: Aikido lists the nine exact RPC hostnames the loader cycles through; correlating them with a Node/npm/Python/VS Code parent process distinguishes GlassWorm activity from legitimate Solana developers (who would not generally hit all nine within a short polling loop and would not initiate from a preinstall hook). Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/glassworm-chrome-extension-rat
ATT&CKT1102.001 T1568.002 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (SolanaRpc)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","npm-cli.js","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","python.exe","py.exe","code.exe","electron.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","code.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc

ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where DnsQuery has_any (SolanaRpc)
| where SrcUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName, EventProduct, EventVendor
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] GlassWorm Stage-3a Ledger impersonator binary execution (SHA256 06fab21d / SKuyzYcDD.exe) Actions on Objectives High
Detects execution of the .NET WPF Ledger Live / Trezor impersonator dropped by GlassWorm's Stage-3a, either by SHA256 06fab21dc276e3ab9b5d0a1532398979fd377b080c86d74f2c53a04603a43b1d or by the drop name SKuyzYcDD.exe in %TEMP%, or by the signed-binary metadata strings Assaac.exe / LLC LogicSub. Rationale: SHA256 06fab21d... and the drop name SKuyzYcDD.exe are explicit IOCs from the Aikido article; the LLC LogicSub / Assaac.exe publisher and original-filename strings are unique and survive renames. Combining four orthogonal anchors (hash, drop name, %TEMP% path, signed metadata) keeps the detection resilient to single-IOC rotation. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/glassworm-chrome-extension-rat
ATT&CKT1036.005 T1657 T1555
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where SHA256 == "06fab21dc276e3ab9b5d0a1532398979fd377b080c86d74f2c53a04603a43b1d"
   or FileName =~ "SKuyzYcDD.exe"
   or (FolderPath has @"\Temp\" and FileName endswith ".exe" and ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "Assaac.exe")
   or ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName =~ "LLC LogicSub"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine, ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName, ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SHA256 == "06fab21dc276e3ab9b5d0a1532398979fd377b080c86d74f2c53a04603a43b1d"
   or TargetProcessName endswith @"\SKuyzYcDD.exe"
   or ActingProcessName endswith @"\SKuyzYcDD.exe"
   or (TargetProcessCommandLine has @"\Temp\" and TargetProcessCommandLine has_cs "SKuyzYcDD")
   or ActingProcessFileCompany =~ "LLC LogicSub"
   or TargetProcessFileCompany =~ "LLC LogicSub"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA256, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessFileCompany
| order by TimeGenerated desc

DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email

         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| rename All_Email.recipient as user

    [| tstats `summariesonly` count

        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")

     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count

    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("06fab21dc276e3ab9b5d0a1532398979fd377b080c86d74f2c53a04603a43b1d") or SHA1 in~ ("06fab21dc276e3ab9b5d0a1532398979fd377b080c86d74f2c53a04603a43b1d") or MD5 in~ ("06fab21dc276e3ab9b5d0a1532398979fd377b080c86d74f2c53a04603a43b1d")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("06fab21dc276e3ab9b5d0a1532398979fd377b080c86d74f2c53a04603a43b1d") or SHA1 in~ ("06fab21dc276e3ab9b5d0a1532398979fd377b080c86d74f2c53a04603a43b1d") or MD5 in~ ("06fab21dc276e3ab9b5d0a1532398979fd377b080c86d74f2c53a04603a43b1d")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["06fab21dc276e3ab9b5d0a1532398979fd377b080c86d74f2c53a04603a43b1d"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"

The fast-draft Open VSX extension was compromised to deploy a BlokTrooper RAT and infostealer via GitHub-hosted payloads. Multiple malicious versions identified. Category: Vulnerabilities & Threats

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] VSCode/VSCodium spawning shell or curl to raw.githubusercontent.com/BlokTrooper · [LLM] VSCode-family host fetching from raw.githubusercontent.com/BlokTrooper/extension path
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Four-way node.exe -e fanout spawned from VSCode shell descendants (BlokTrooper stage-2) · Article-specific behavioural hunt — fast-draft Open VSX Extension Compromised by BlokTrooper
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound TCP beacon to BlokTrooper Socket.IO C2 195.201.104.53:6931/6936/6939 · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Non-browser process copying Chrome/Edge/Brave Login Data, Web Data, or wallet extension LevelDB state · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process
[LLM] VSCode/VSCodium spawning shell or curl to raw.githubusercontent.com/BlokTrooper Delivery High
Detects the fast-draft Open VSX delivery primitive: a VSCode-family editor (Code.exe, VSCodium.exe, Cursor.exe) or its bundled node.exe spawning curl/cmd/sh/powershell whose command line references the BlokTrooper staging repo on raw.githubusercontent.com. Hits 0.10.89, 0.10.105, 0.10.106 and 0.10.112 alike. Rationale: Anchors on the exact staging URL fragment 'raw.githubusercontent.com/BlokTrooper' named in the article and ties it to a VSCode-family parent — extension hosts legitimately shell out for many reasons, but never to this attacker-controlled repo. Cross-checked against Aikido write-up plus general supply-chain TTPs. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/fast-draft-open-vsx-bloktrooper • https://open-vsx.org/extension/KhangNghiem/fast-draft • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.003 T1105

title: VSCode Extension Host Fetching BlokTrooper Payload From GitHub
id: 5a3e8c4d-9b7f-4a1c-8e3d-1f2a3b4c5d6e
description: Detects VSCode/VSCodium/Cursor or its bundled node spawning a shell or curl that references raw.githubusercontent.com/BlokTrooper, the staging path used by the compromised KhangNghiem/fast-draft Open VSX extension.
references:
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/fast-draft-open-vsx-bloktrooper
  - https://open-vsx.org/extension/KhangNghiem/fast-draft
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/03/18
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1059.003
  - attack.t1105
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\Code.exe'
      - '\Code - Insiders.exe'
      - '\VSCodium.exe'
      - '\Cursor.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\bash.exe'
      - '\sh.exe'
      - '\wsl.exe'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'raw.githubusercontent.com'
      - 'BlokTrooper'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\Code.exe OR *\code.exe OR *\VSCodium.exe OR *\Cursor.exe OR *\node.exe) @Image:(*\curl.exe OR *\cmd.exe OR *\powershell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\bash.exe OR *\sh.exe OR *\wsl.exe) @CommandLine:(*raw.githubusercontent.com* AND *BlokTrooper*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(Code|Code - Insiders|VSCodium|Cursor|node)\.exe$/i ImageFileName=/(curl|cmd|powershell|pwsh|bash|sh|wsl)\.exe$/i
| regex("raw\.githubusercontent\.com", field=CommandLine)
| regex("BlokTrooper", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)

[LLM] Outbound TCP beacon to BlokTrooper Socket.IO C2 195.201.104.53:6931/6936/6939 Command & Control High
Catches the stage-2 RAT / stealer / file-exfil / clipboard modules connecting back to the article-named Hetzner-hosted C2 on ports 6931, 6936 and 6939. Pure IOC match with no FPs in clean environments. Rationale: IP 195.201.104.53 and ports 6931/6936/6939 are explicitly named in the Aikido analysis as the BlokTrooper Socket.IO C2 endpoints reconstructed from the obfuscated octet config. No legitimate enterprise traffic to that Hetzner host on those bespoke ports. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/fast-draft-open-vsx-bloktrooper • https://www.virustotal.com/gui/ip-address/195.201.104.53
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1095

DeviceNetworkEvents

| where RemotePort in (6931, 6936, 6939)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, LocalPort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp asc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr == "195.201.104.53"
| where DstPortNumber in (6931, 6936, 6939)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, NetworkBytes, DvcAction

[LLM] Four-way node.exe -e fanout spawned from VSCode shell descendants (BlokTrooper stage-2) Installation High
The deobfuscated wrapper spawns exactly four detached node.exe processes with -e (inline script) and windowsHide+detached options, one per module (RAT, browser stealer, file exfil, clipboard). Detects ≥4 node -e children of shell processes that ultimately descend from a VSCode editor inside a 5-minute window. Rationale: Four-detached-children pattern is straight from the deobfuscated stage-2 wrapper quoted in the article ('M(..., ["-e", ab], {windowsHide:true, detached:true})' repeated as ab/ac/ad/ae). Threshold 4 matches the exact module count (RAT, browser+wallet stealer, file exfil, clipboard) and is far above benign node -e invocation rates. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/fast-draft-open-vsx-bloktrooper
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1106 T1564.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "node.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\s-e\s"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","wsl.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("Code.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","VSCodium.exe","Cursor.exe","node.exe")
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", "/tmp/", "BlokTrooper", @"\.npm\")
| summarize NodeChildCount = count(), SampleCmds = make_set(ProcessCommandLine, 6), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where NodeChildCount >= 4
| order by FirstSeen desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\node.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\s-e\s"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","wsl.exe")
| summarize NodeChildCount = count(), SampleCmds = make_set(CommandLine, 6), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where NodeChildCount >= 4
| order by FirstSeen desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\node.exe OR *\Node.exe) @CommandLine:(*" -e "* OR *"-e "*) @ParentImage:(*\cmd.exe OR *\powershell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\bash.exe OR *\sh.exe OR *\wsl.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\node\.exe$/i
| regex("\\s-e\\s", field=CommandLine)
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(cmd|powershell|pwsh|bash|sh|wsl)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
| count >= 4
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

| where count >= 4

| tstats summariesonly=false count values(Processes.process) as cmds min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="node.exe" AND Processes.process="* -e *" AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","wsl.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name _time span=5m

[LLM] Non-browser process copying Chrome/Edge/Brave Login Data, Web Data, or wallet extension LevelDB state Actions on Objectives High
Detects the stage-2 browser-and-wallet stealer module (module 2 in the article) — any non-browser process touching Login Data / Login Data For Account / Web Data / Local State / Cookies, or the Local Extension Settings LevelDB used by MetaMask, Phantom, TronLink, Trust Wallet, Coinbase, OKX, Solflare, Rabby, Keplr, UniSat, Enkrypt, Bitget, SafePal, TON Wallet, Petra, Pontem, Nami and Sender. Rationale: File set is exactly what the article enumerates for the stealer module — Login Data, Login Data For Account, Web Data, plus the LevelDB state under \Local Extension Settings\ that holds the 25 named wallet extensions. Excluding the browser binaries that legitimately own these files leaves only stealer behaviour as a residual. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/fast-draft-open-vsx-bloktrooper • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
ATT&CKT1555.003 T1539 T1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FileName in~ ("Login Data","Login Data For Account","Web Data","Local State","Cookies"))
    or (FolderPath has @"\Local Extension Settings\")
    or (PreviousFileName in~ ("Login Data","Login Data For Account","Web Data","Local State","Cookies"))
    or (PreviousFolderPath has @"\Local Extension Settings\")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","opera_gx.exe","explorer.exe","MsMpEng.exe","MsSense.exe","MpDefenderCoreService.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, PreviousFolderPath, PreviousFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data", "Login Data For Account", "Web Data", "Local State", "Cookies")
    or TargetFilePath has @"\Local Extension Settings\"
| where not (ActingProcessName has_any ("chrome.exe", "msedge.exe", "brave.exe", "opera.exe", "opera_gx.exe", "explorer.exe", "MsMpEng.exe", "MsSense.exe", "SearchProtocolHost.exe"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType, DvcAction
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Non-Browser Process Accessing Chromium Login Data Or Wallet Extension LevelDB
id: 8e7f1b2c-4d5e-6f7a-8b9c-0d1e2f3a4b5c
description: Detects the BlokTrooper stage-2 browser and wallet stealer module — a non-browser process touching Chrome/Edge/Brave/Opera Login Data, Login Data For Account, Web Data, Local State, Cookies, or any wallet extension Local Extension Settings LevelDB store (MetaMask, Phantom, TronLink, Trust Wallet, Coinbase, OKX, Solflare, Rabby, Keplr, UniSat, Enkrypt, Bitget, SafePal, TON Wallet, Petra, Pontem, Nami, Sender).
references:
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/fast-draft-open-vsx-bloktrooper
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/03/18
tags:
  - attack.t1555.003
  - attack.t1539
  - attack.t1005
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_files:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '\Login Data'
      - '\Login Data For Account'
      - '\Web Data'
      - '\Local State'
      - '\Cookies'
  selection_wallet:
    TargetFilename|contains: '\Local Extension Settings\'
  filter_browser:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\chrome.exe'
      - '\msedge.exe'
      - '\brave.exe'
      - '\opera.exe'
      - '\opera_gx.exe'
  filter_av:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\MsMpEng.exe'
      - '\MsSense.exe'
      - '\explorer.exe'
      - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
  condition: (selection_files or selection_wallet) and not (filter_browser or filter_av)
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:*"Login Data"* OR @TargetFilename:*"Web Data"* OR @TargetFilename:*"Local State"* OR @TargetFilename:*"Cookies"* OR @TargetFilename:*"Local Extension Settings"*) -@Image:(*\chrome.exe OR *\msedge.exe OR *\brave.exe OR *\opera.exe OR *\opera_gx.exe OR *\MsMpEng.exe OR *\MsSense.exe OR *\explorer.exe)
#event_simpleName=/^(FileWritten|FileOpenInfo)$/ (TargetFileName=/\\Login Data$/i OR TargetFileName=/\\Login Data For Account$/i OR TargetFileName=/\\Web Data$/i OR TargetFileName=/\\Local State$/i OR TargetFileName=/\\Cookies$/i OR regex("\\\\Local Extension Settings\\\\", field=TargetFileName))
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\(chrome|msedge|brave|opera|opera_gx|MsMpEng|MsSense|explorer)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process_name) as proc values(Filesystem.process) as cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name IN ("Login Data","Login Data For Account","Web Data","Local State","Cookies") OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Local Extension Settings\\*") AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","MsMpEng.exe","explorer.exe","MsSense.exe") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process_name) as proc values(Filesystem.process) as cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name IN ("Login Data","Login Data For Account","Web Data","Local State","Cookies") OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Local Extension Settings\\*") AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","MsMpEng.exe","explorer.exe","MsSense.exe") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("195.201.104.53") or RemoteUrl has_any ("raw.githubusercontent.com/BlokTrooper/extension")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["195.201.104.53"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["raw.githubusercontent.com/BlokTrooper/extension"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)

| order by TimeGenerated desc

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

[LLM] Glassworm stage-2/stage-3 C2 callback to 45.32.150.251 or 217.69.3.152 Command & Control High
Detects outbound HTTP from any host to the two attacker-controlled IPs hosting the Glassworm stage-2 decryptor and stage-3 stealer C2 endpoints (/get_arhive_npm/, /wall). These IPs are unique to this campaign and any contact is a high-fidelity indicator that a developer or CI runner installed the backdoored react-native-country-select@0.3.91 or react-native-international-phone-number@0.11.8 package. Rationale: Both /16-unique IPs are explicitly named in the article as stage-2 fetch host (45.32.150.251) and stage-3 exfil endpoint (217.69.3.152:80/wall). URL fragments get_arhive_npm and 3e4Tg8V are unique slug patterns from the recovered payloads. Single hit = compromise.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1195.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
let GlassWormIPs = dynamic(["45.32.150.251","217.69.3.152"]);
let GlassWormUrlMarkers = dynamic(["get_arhive_npm","3e4Tg8V","/wall"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (GlassWormIPs)
   or (isnotempty(RemoteUrl) and RemoteUrl has_any (GlassWormUrlMarkers))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
let GlassWormIPs = dynamic(["45.32.150.251","217.69.3.152"]);
let GlassWormUrlMarkers = dynamic(["get_arhive_npm","3e4Tg8V","/wall"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DestinationIP in (GlassWormIPs)
       or (isnotempty(RequestURL) and RequestURL has_any (GlassWormUrlMarkers))
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestURL, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, DeviceAction),
  (ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DstIpAddr in (GlassWormIPs) or (isnotempty(Url) and Url has_any (GlassWormUrlMarkers))
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, DvcAction)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Glassworm stage-3 persistence: schtasks UpdateApp + HKCU Run DPKCbbQ Installation High
Detects the dual-persistence pattern dropped by the Glassworm stage-3 stealer: a scheduled task named 'UpdateApp' with /sc onstart /rl highest running a hidden PowerShell, and an HKCU Run key named 'DPKCbbQ'. Both indicators are hard-coded in the recovered payload and unlikely to collide with legitimate software. Rationale: The literal task name 'UpdateApp', Run value 'DPKCbbQ', /sc onstart with /rl highest, and hidden-bypass powershell launcher are all directly quoted from the recovered stage-3 script. They are arbitrary attacker-chosen strings and collide with no known legitimate software.
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1547.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Registry
let TaskPersistence = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "schtasks.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "UpdateApp"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "onstart"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Bypass","-rl highest")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Indicator="schtasks_UpdateApp";
let RegPersistence = DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has @"\CurrentVersion\Run"
| where RegistryValueName =~ "DPKCbbQ"
   or RegistryValueData has @"powershell" and RegistryValueData has "WindowStyle Hidden" and RegistryValueData has "Bypass"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName,
          RegistryValueData, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Indicator="HKCU_Run_DPKCbbQ";
union TaskPersistence, RegPersistence
| order by Timestamp desc
let TaskPersistence = SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\schtasks.exe"
| where CommandLine has "UpdateApp"
| where CommandLine has "onstart"
| where CommandLine has_any ("Bypass","highest")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName, Indicator="schtasks_UpdateApp";
let RegPersistence = ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where RegistryKey has @"\CurrentVersion\Run"
| where RegistryValue =~ "DPKCbbQ"
   or (RegistryValueData has "powershell" and RegistryValueData has "WindowStyle Hidden" and RegistryValueData has "Bypass")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey,
          RegistryValue, RegistryValueData,
          ActingProcessName, Indicator="HKCU_Run_DPKCbbQ";
union TaskPersistence, RegPersistence
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Glassworm side-staged Node.js runtime under %APPDATA%\_node_x86 / _node_x64 Installation High
Detects the distinctive Glassworm stage-3 behaviour of downloading the full Node.js v22.9.0 Windows runtime ZIP from nodejs.org and unpacking it under %APPDATA%\_node_x86 or %APPDATA%\_node_x64. The stealer ships its own Node runtime so it can execute the payload on hosts without Node installed; these exact folder names are hard-coded. Rationale: The folder names _node_x86 and _node_x64 under %APPDATA% are literal strings in the recovered stage-3 JavaScript, as is the pinned Node.js v22.9.0 download URL. Legitimate Node installers do not place runtimes there — these are attacker-chosen sandbox staging directories.
ATT&CKT1105 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Web.Web
let SideStageFolders = dynamic([@"\AppData\Roaming\_node_x86\", @"\AppData\Roaming\_node_x64\"]);
let NodeZips = dynamic(["node-v22.9.0-win-x86.zip","node-v22.9.0-win-x64.zip"]);
let FileSig = DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has_any (SideStageFolders) or FileName in~ (NodeZips)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, Indicator="appdata_node_runtime";
let NetSig = DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "nodejs.org/download/release/v22.9.0/node-v22.9.0-win"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, Indicator="nodejs_zip_download_nonbrowser";
union FileSig, NetSig
| order by Timestamp desc
let SideStageFolders = dynamic([@"\AppData\Roaming\_node_x86\", @"\AppData\Roaming\_node_x64\"]);
let NodeZips = dynamic(["node-v22.9.0-win-x86.zip","node-v22.9.0-win-x64.zip"]);
let FileSig = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (SideStageFolders) or TargetFileName in~ (NodeZips)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath,
          TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          ActorUsername, Indicator="appdata_node_runtime";
let NetSig = ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Url has "nodejs.org/download/release/v22.9.0/node-v22.9.0-win"
| where HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent !has "Chrome" and HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent !has "Firefox" and HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent !has "Edg/"
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, Url,
          HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, DstIpAddr, Indicator="nodejs_zip_download_nonbrowser";
union FileSig, NetSig
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("45.32.150.251", "217.69.3.152") or RemoteUrl has_any ("")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["45.32.150.251", "217.69.3.152"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic([""]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Suspicious browser extension installation Installation Medium

title: Browser Extension Installation via Registry
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0a
status: experimental
description: |
    Registry writes under the browser extension policy keys —
    administrative install of an extension. Often used by adware /
    info-stealers to bypass user-level extension controls.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1176/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1176
    - attack.persistence

detection:

        TargetObject|contains:
            - '\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\'
            - '\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\'
            - '\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:

level: medium
ENDPOINT

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\*")
    by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.registry_value_name, Registry.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
    where (Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\*")

| `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

title: Crypto-Wallet Keystore Access by Non-Wallet Process
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d02
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers / wallet drainers read keystore files from MetaMask,
    Exodus, Atomic, Phantom, Bitcoin, Electrum, Ethereum-cli wallets.
    Filtering out the legitimate wallet binaries leaves only attacker
    activity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1005/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1005
    - attack.collection
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Ethereum\keystore\'
            - '\Bitcoin\'
            - '\Exodus\'
            - '\Electrum\wallets\'
            - '\MetaMask\'
            - '\Phantom\'
            - '\Atomic\Local Storage\'
    filter_legit:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\MetaMask.exe'
            - '\Exodus.exe'
            - '\Atomic.exe'
            - '\electrum.exe'
            - '\Bitcoin.exe'
            - '\Phantom.exe'

falsepositives:

level: high

        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

title: Scheduled Task Creation with Suspicious Image / Encoded Args
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0d

description: |
